# ACT

Imitation learning policy that predicts action chunks with a transformer and executes them over short horizons.

<div class="algorithm-meta">
  <span>Learning</span>
  <span>imitation learning, transformers, action chunking</span>
  <span>Mermaid</span>
</div>

## Flowchart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Collect teleoperated demonstrations] --> B[Build observation and action-chunk dataset]
    B --> C[Encode current observations]
    C --> D[Transformer predicts K-step action chunk]
    D --> E[Compare predicted chunk with demonstrated actions]
    E --> F[Update policy with behavior cloning loss]
    F --> G{Training complete?}
    G -- No --> B
    G -- Yes --> H[Deploy policy on robot]
    H --> I[Observe current state]
    I --> J[Predict next action chunk]
    J --> K[Execute first action or temporal ensemble]
    K --> L{Task complete?}
    L -- No --> I
    L -- Yes --> M[Stop]
```

## Formulas

### Behavior cloning objective

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{BC}} = \mathbb{E}_{(o_t, a_{t:t+K-1})}\!\left[\left\lVert \hat{a}_{t:t+K-1} - a_{t:t+K-1}\right\rVert_1\right]
$$

### Chunked policy

$$
\hat{a}_{t:t+K-1} = \pi_\theta(o_t, z)
$$

## Notes

- ACT stands for Action Chunking with Transformers.
- Predicting several future actions at once reduces compounding error and allows smoother closed-loop execution.
- A latent variable or encoder can model demonstration variability when multiple valid action chunks exist.
